checks.required: Close both frontends → Host remains running; native pub/sub still works
Browser uses loopback HTTP/1.1 → Full functionality without browser HTTP/3 certificate requirements
Send an HTML-looking text payload → Displayed as text in both clients
Backup and official restore → Domain/images/receipts coherent; epoch rotates; clients resynchronize
Same end-to-end scenario in WinUI and web → Equivalent objects, ownership, targets, threads, and errors
Switch profile while a send is unresolved → Original caller retained; no relabelled send/subscription
Fragment SSE across arbitrary byte boundaries → Correct UTF-8/frame parsing and cursor advancement
Clean supported Windows VM → Self-contained host/WinUI start; webapp works without Node/CDN
Select another profile without credentials → Same creation/viewing abilities; ownership adds no privilege
Cross-origin web form/fetch/image attempts → API origin/header protections hold; same-origin app still works
Shutdown during normal operation → Bounded drain; surviving committed commands recover by receipt
Windows proxy/PAC configured → Supplied local clients and readiness probe still connect directly to loopback

criteria.required: A fresh checkout restores pinned dependencies and builds every introduced project in Release with zero build/restore/analyzer warnings.
The actual host process starts and exits cleanly; an actual WinUI window opens and closes on the declared Windows target.
The scenario harness is runnable and reports environment, candidate commit, command, exit status, and unimplemented capability state.
The verifier rejects unknown IDs and unimplemented checks; it cannot report a missing runner or skipped execution as PASS.
Product web assets need no frontend framework or Node dependency; no domain feature is falsely declared complete.
Every valid fixture round-trips without loss and every invalid discriminator, unknown request property, or contradictory selector fails predictably.
UUIDs, string-encoded sequences, UTC timestamps, caller bootstrap rules, and receipt versus subscription state match the specification.
Canonical image request hashing inputs are documented as normalized request fields plus verified image-byte digest; boundary and filename do not change identity.
Omitted/default/empty option normalization is deterministic; target-ID ordering does not produce a different canonical request hash.
Fixture execution calls the actual contract code and exits nonzero on a mismatch; no required contract field is inferred from a shortened example.
The messaging probe uses RequestVersionExact=3.0 and verifies response.Version=3.0; a TCP-only port check is never accepted as QUIC proof.
Frontend HTTP/1.1 responds independently; the browser is not required to trust a self-signed HTTP/3 certificate.
Wrong pin, hostname mismatch, expiry, unavailable QUIC, and occupied configured ports fail clearly with no false-ready descriptor.
A restart loads a persisted private key and native clients reject arbitrary certificates; no accept-any validation is present.
The self-probe runs after server binding and bypasses configured Windows proxy/PAC settings.
Probe results are marked supporting transport evidence, not final completion of persisted-publication A03 or durable-subscription A04.
Valid-authority wrong-surface requests return 404; invalid authority returns 400; Host spoofing cannot switch surfaces.
Static/default assets are available only on the frontend listener.
Cross-origin/null-Origin browser mutations and simple form posts without required header are rejected before any handler side effect.
Same-origin browser fetch and native requests with the required header succeed through permitted routes.
No wildcard CORS, all-interface binding, unsafe forwarded-host trust, or unbounded request parsing is introduced.
Starting with an empty directory applies migrations; reopening preserves the same store epoch, schema, and data.
A competing host cannot independently use the same store; unrelated occupied ports/data are not overwritten.
Effective SQLite FK, WAL, synchronous, and timeout settings match the design and are verified using the real provider.
Required FK/composite-parent/root/unique/check constraints exist and are exercised with real SQLite fixtures.
Migration or initialization failure prevents application readiness and never silently recreates the store; EnsureCreated is not mixed with migrations.
Contexts and connections are not shared across concurrent units of work; readiness descriptor contains the actual persistent epoch.
Valid PNG/JPEG files decode completely and produce verified format, dimensions, byte length, and SHA-256 metadata.
The runner works in the unpackaged headless host context without HWND/MSIX/WinUI dependence.
Disallowed type, malformed data, animation, excessive bytes/dimensions/pixels, and arithmetic overflow are rejected.
Concurrency is bounded at two validations and buffers/native resources are released after success or failure.
Component evidence is labeled supporting A31 evidence; the full persisted image API is not claimed complete until T016.
One valid command creates exactly one user, one user.created event, and one committed receipt.
Same normalized request ID/payload returns the same user and event count, including after restart.
Changed payload/caller/operation under an existing request ID returns 409 without writes.
Handle normalization and uniqueness, bounds, and null/absent caller rules behave exactly as specified.
Both surfaces use one handler and equivalent contracts; selecting/creating a user requires no authentication.
Targets/parents/images/coupled-subscribe features not implemented yet cannot be silently ignored by other command variants.
Every accepted channel create produces exactly one channel and one initial session, both owned by the caller.
A supplied first-session title is preserved; omission uses General.
The event order is channel then session; the receipt distinguishes resolved objects from newly created objects.
Any invalid initial-session/channel input rolls back all objects, events, and receipt.
Same-request retries return original IDs; unknown caller IDs do not create users or containers implicitly.
The new IDs are queryable through both surfaces and are suitable subscription scopes once subscriptions are implemented.
User B can create a session in A's channel; the channel remains owned by A and the new session is owned by B.
A session command selecting a new channel creates one channel and exactly one session.
Unknown existing channel IDs return 404; conflicting selector fields are rejected without implicit creation.
All objects/events/receipt commit atomically with stable IDs on retry.
Any logical user has the same create/view capabilities regardless of recorded owner.
Existing channel/session text creates only the message; new-session and new-channel forms create the intended graph with correct ownership.
Root messages have null parent, own root ID, depth 1, caller author, and committed string sequence.
Invalid or mismatched existing references, whitespace-only text, oversize input, and unauthorized write fields leave zero partial writes.
Channel/session/message creation events are ordered and invisible before commit.
Retrying an unchanged request returns original IDs and does not append new events.
Nonempty targets, parent IDs, image content, or coupled subscription options remain explicitly unavailable until their implementing task passes.
A genuine H3 command commits a message and reports response.Version 3.0; querying the stored message proves the real handler was used.
The same command retried through F returns the same created IDs and no extra rows/events.
Receipt queries return committed state and operation; no visible receipt maps to request_not_committed without proving a request could never commit.
Location/relative paths derive from the configured accepted surface and cannot be poisoned by Host.
Errors and body validation are consistent across M/F; normal-operation diagnostics are clean.
Failure before commit leaves no graph/receipt/event; failure after commit returns the original result on retry.
Concurrent identical requests yield one committed result; conflicting uses of the same ID yield deterministic conflict.
Concurrent distinct requests remain consistent with required FKs, event order, and no shared-context errors.
Write wait/provider timeout is finite and returns the specified retryable error while preserving the original retry identity.
The fault scenario runs repeatedly with explicit synchronization points, not timing-only sleeps; expected injected failures are distinguished from unexpected diagnostics.
Users, channels, and sessions can be listed and retrieved through both surfaces with correct independent owner fields.
Paging at H neither includes later creations nor skips/duplicates eligible earlier objects.
Page tokens preserve the snapshot/filter/order and reject malformed or wrong-epoch data.
Default/max page sizes are enforced; any counts use the same H.
Catalog tests are supporting snapshot evidence; full snapshot-plus-replay A23 remains open until T024.
Known handles and explicit IDs produce one canonical target set; duplicate sources create one MessageTargets row.
Unknown syntactically valid handles or nonexistent explicit IDs fail the complete compound request with the specified error.
Escaped/email/invalid-short/overlong/leading-digit cases follow the exact frozen grammar.
Mentions history returns each targeted message once with correct ordering/snapshot semantics.
Other logical users still see the message in session history; targeting adds routing and does not imply privacy.
Caption targeting uses the same parser when image commands become available; no second inconsistent parser is introduced.
Root/reply/nested reply produce depths 1/2/3 and correct common root IDs.
Replying to level 3 or a message in another session fails with zero object/event/receipt writes.
Clients cannot override author, depth, root, or timestamps.
Small thread pages return needed ancestors without inventing detached roots or duplicating context.
Replies have only their own explicit/textual targets and remain publicly viewable.
Self-root insertion and composite parent/root FKs work against real SQLite, not only mocked storage.
Valid PNG/JPEG messages work in existing/new container combinations and return bytes matching the stored digest.
The 8 MiB binary/9 MiB request, dimension/pixel, part-count, and decoder bounds are enforced with actionable errors.
Invalid image/target/parent input leaves no orphan image or partially created conversation.
Equivalent retries with the same bytes and canonical JSON return the original result despite filename/boundary changes; changed bytes conflict.
Event, receipt, and history JSON contain descriptors only; no binary/base64 or local file path leaks.
Image content is fetched after bounded database materialization and response concurrency never exceeds the configured limit.
Root and flat views return their specified membership/order; all detail/history DTOs agree for the same message.
Queries at H exclude later roots/replies and counts use H; continuation never loses or duplicates eligible messages.
Thread context is bounded to required ancestors and does not consume the requested item limit.
Image-bearing rows are projected without fetching BLOB bytes for ordinary history.
Query/page limits and epoch/head checks are enforced before materializing unbounded data.
Navigation by a message ID resolves its proper thread/session even when its root is outside the current history page.
OpenAPI and returned objects agree on required fields, discriminators, sequence encoding, receipt operation/state, and content shapes.
Every specified content/query route is reachable on its correct surface and guarded before handler execution.
No domain PATCH/PUT/DELETE operation exists; unsupported methods receive the documented outcome.
Multipart and JSON requests enforce declared limits, origin/header rules, and stable Problem Details across M/F.
Image bytes stay out of all JSON contracts; caller-supplied server-owned fields are rejected.
The executable matrix fails on a missing route/schema check and leaves the current cumulative build runnable.
Create returns an inspectable persisted definition and correct numeric start head for each supported mode.
Subscription definition and historical receipt survive restart; create/close retries do not create extra subscriptions.
Close preserves queryable metadata; new consumption returns 410, and mismatched supplied closer is rejected by the specified correctness rule.
Unknown filter IDs, empty filters, malformed/future/wrong-epoch cursors, and oversized filter sets fail correctly.
Create/close does not generate domain events; a closed historical subscription is not recreated by a command retry.
Live connection count is zero when no stream is attached and is explicitly transient rather than a delivery acknowledgement.
Overlapping branches return one logical event in ascending sequence order.
An empty sparse page can advance nextCursor; iteration reaches the captured head without repeated scanning or missed matches.
No nextCursor skips a matching event excluded by count or byte budget.
At most 1,000 headers, requested bounded items, and 1 MiB matching payloads are processed per batch; one allowed event can always make progress.
All cursor error codes and conflicting cursor inputs behave as specified.
Image events carry descriptors only and no query retains a context while a consumer waits.
Channel creation can resolve its automatically created initial session; session/message variants resolve their selected/new containers correctly.
beforeRequest starts before the command's own events, allowing relevant creation events to be queried.
An invalid coupled scope or any failing object validation leaves no subscription or partial graph.
A replay returns the original subscription reference even if it is now closed; it never reopens/replaces it.
Request ID conflicts are enforced across object create, subscription create, and close, including nullable bootstrap caller.
User bootstrap rejects subscribe; ordinary sends can omit it without creating a new saved subscription.
Exact-H3 subscription responses have Version 3.0 and deliver actual committed events after transaction commit.
Frontend consumers receive equivalent event framing and payloads over HTTP/1.1.
Replay transitions to live delivery without skipping events; channel subscriptions include future sessions and catalog subscriptions see new containers.
Checkpoint IDs advance only after prior matching events are flushed; comments/control events obey their cursor rules.
Quiet streams receive heartbeats, and cancellation disposes stream resources.
No context/reader/transaction is kept open while waiting for a client, and established SSE does not receive an appended JSON error document.
Two consumers of one subscription replay independently; no shared cursor causes one to steal events.
A close/attach race cannot leave an indefinitely live closed subscription; already transmitted frames are handled according to documented semantics.
A slow/stalled receiver is bounded/closed, releases resources, and cannot indefinitely block ordinary publishers.
Commit-after-empty-read and crash-after-commit-before-wake scenarios lose no committed matching event after recovery.
Registry counts return to baseline after detach/timeout; query metadata reports actual current connections.
Actual subscription/stream routes preserve listener isolation and deduplicate overlapping filters.
The deterministic scenarios use synchronization hooks confined to verification tooling and produce no unexpected normal-operation warnings.
The same client supports F and explicit M mode, with actual exact-H3 evidence and no proxy detour.
Uncertain text/image/coupled sends retry the original caller/request/payload and reconcile the committed result.
Snapshot plus concurrent publication/replay produces the complete committed view without duplicate applied messages.
Split UTF-8/CRLF/multiline frames parse correctly; keepalive bytes prevent false idle reconnects.
There is one reconnect loop per subscription with bounded jitter/backoff, cancellation, and Retry-After handling.
Epoch mismatch/future cursor/closed subscription produces explicit resynchronization rather than a silent wait.
The runnable sample uses real host/SQLite behavior; parser-only fixtures are supporting evidence for later dual-frontend A41 closure.
An empty store offers Create User and the selected profile is retrieved again after reload without any login flow.
Channel/session directories are queryable and owner labels remain distinct.
All API requests include the required header and same-origin policy; no CDN/framework/Node runtime is required.
Message/user-provided labels are rendered through safe text nodes; browser console has no unexpected errors/warnings.
The active caller is per tab; another tab's localStorage change cannot switch it automatically.
A creates exactly one initial session with a new channel; B creates a session there without changing the channel owner.
Sent root text persists, reloads, and displays author/targets/content through canonical DTOs.
Uncertain retries reuse the same request identity; editing a failed draft allocates a new ID.
Validation failures preserve the draft and show field-specific errors; Sent means committed, not read/delivered.
HTML-looking content renders literally and never creates executable DOM.
Loaded root pages remain bounded and chronological display does not corrupt pagination order.
Root/reply/nested reply render as three levels; Reply is disabled at level 3 and backend rejection is still surfaced.
Pagination supplies missing ancestors and never displays a nested reply as a new root.
Known mentions/explicit targets display consistently; unknown recognized handles preserve the draft and show their error.
Mentions show only matching targets for the selected profile; public session history remains visible to others.
Reply targets are not silently inherited; target chips derive from canonical server IDs.
The flow remains keyboard-usable with visible focus and labelled controls.
Valid PNG/JPEG with optional caption sends and reloads from the persisted image content route.
Invalid/oversized content produces the server error and preserves the editable draft.
Retries use unchanged bytes/caller/request ID even when the transport multipart boundary changes.
Ordinary JSON/event/history contains descriptors only, with no base64 or file path.
Object URLs and obsolete image loads are disposed, and concurrent fetching stays bounded.
No returned text or image filename is inserted as unsafe HTML.
Split UTF-8 and CR/LF/CRLF/multiline SSE fixtures and real streams apply correctly; heartbeat comments keep quiet connections alive.
Publishing during initial load and response/event reordering produce a complete view with one visible canonical message.
Profile switches never relabel pending sends; closing the old subscription does not affect other clients.
Another tab's storage events cannot change the active caller, and cloned/reloaded tabs do not take exclusive ownership of a shared subscription.
Connection loss shows useful state; reconnect is bounded, honors Retry-After, and stops on cancellation or unsupported contract.
Store-epoch change clears scoped state, revalidates profile IDs, and reloads history.
The browser completes every implemented feature using the frontend listener without browser HTTP/3 dependence.
The native app opens on the qualified Windows target and creates/selects real profiles without authentication.
Catalog data and ownership come from API DTOs; the native process never opens SQLite.
UI interaction remains responsive during network work and obsolete loads are cancelled.
Closing the native window disposes its connection work without stopping the host.
Unavailable host errors are actionable and do not launch any path supplied by untrusted endpoint metadata.
Basic focus order, control labels, and keyboard navigation work.
Native channel creation produces exactly one initial session; B's new session does not change A's channel ownership.
Committed text survives reopening and is rendered literally, including HTML-looking input.
An uncertain retry produces one committed/visible message with its original author and request ID.
Validation failures preserve drafts and show specific errors; an edited draft receives a new request ID.
Network/image-independent background work does not block the dispatcher or leave obsolete selection results in the active view.
Three total message levels render correctly and level-4 replies are unavailable/rejected.
A nested message reached from Mentions resolves the correct thread without creating a false root.
Canonical target IDs, unknown-handle errors, and reply target behavior match the shared contract scenario; replies do not inherit targets.
Other profiles retain visibility of targeted conversation history.
The native UI uses the same contracts and no extra ownership restrictions.
Keyboard operation and focus remain usable through target selection and reply cancellation.
The picker works in the unpackaged WinUI app and valid PNG/JPEG messages send and reload.
Errors from invalid/oversized files preserve the draft and show the server's reason.
Retry identity includes the unchanged image bytes, original caller, and request ID.
No image BLOB is fetched through ordinary JSON, and no UI-thread database/network blocking is introduced.
Image objects/streams are disposed when no longer needed, with bounded concurrent loads.
Native image behavior matches the shared image contract, validation corpus, and payload limits.
Publishing during initial load or reconnect yields complete canonical state with no duplicate visible messages.
Quiet heartbeats remain healthy because liveness tracks bytes/comments, not only parsed domain events.
Switching profiles never changes an in-flight caller or closes another client's subscription.
Changing conversation cancels obsolete loads and cannot overwrite a newly selected conversation.
Store-epoch mismatch triggers profile revalidation and a fresh snapshot.
One native reconnect loop exists per active subscription and shutdown disposes it.
The native frontend and a second T024 sample consumer operate together with independent cursor positions.
Host starts and serves real commands/subscriptions with no UI open; closing both UIs leaves exact-H3 messaging operational.
WinUI starts only the bundled known executable; endpoint metadata cannot choose an arbitrary executable.
Duplicate launch reuses one valid host; stale descriptor/conflicting port/lock produces useful failure instead of overwrite or port drift.
Optional sign-in startup changes only on an explicit operator choice and can be removed.
Stop responds then performs a bounded drain; known committed work can be reconciled after restart.
Direct-loopback clients/probes remain correct with proxy/PAC settings; user-logoff survival is not claimed.
Backup contains coherent entities, images, receipts, and events; an active store cannot be replaced.
Before-publication interruption leaves the old usable history/epoch; after publication the restored history always has its new epoch.
No old sidecar can be applied to the replacement, and a failed validation/replace preserves the current store or documented recoverable safety backup.
Normal restart does not rotate epoch; official restore closes restored active subscriptions.
Both frontends and native client detect the new epoch, revalidate profile IDs, and reload instead of silently waiting on stale cursors.
The maintenance command clearly reports manual-file-replacement limits and never silently discards the current store.
Status reflects the actual effective configuration and observed probe state rather than configured intent.
Invalid values and port/certificate/lock/migration/storage failures prevent false readiness with actionable diagnostics.
Logs omit message text, image bytes, complete request bodies, file-picker paths, and private-key material.
Log growth is bounded, stream counts return to baseline, and normal operation emits no unexpected warnings.
Timeout handling remains finite and uses provider behavior without unlimited retry wrappers.
There is no silent protocol fallback, new-store reset, or warning suppression to conceal a problem.
Both runtime families and required native/static files are present; product execution does not require a development SDK or Node/CDN.
The package records exact source commit, dependency versions, target platform, configuration, and artifact hashes.
Publication succeeds with zero build/publish/packaging warnings and excludes test hooks/private keys/user data.
Replacing application binaries does not overwrite the existing database or selected data directory.
The actual published host/WinUI launch and expose the same contracts, limits, and version described by the manifest.
Run/stop/backup/restore instructions match the packaged command interfaces.
The documented dataset/scenarios are reproducible and bounded without modifying production semantics or public fault routes.
Every retained committed matching event is recoverable, no uncommitted data appears, and duplicate client application is prevented.
Slow streams do not retain database readers, indefinitely block writers, or exceed configured stream/write/payload limits.
Finite contention and close/attach behavior remain correct; stream/connection/native-image resources return to their expected baseline.
Results report measured values and the exact environment; no unmeasured performance promise is asserted.
Expected injected failure diagnostics are asserted separately; all unexpected warnings/findings are resolved before the task passes.
The actual packaged product runs on a clean Windows 11 x64 machine without a development SDK, Node, or external script/CDN dependency.
WinUI and browser complete the same full scenario and produce equivalent persisted objects, owner fields, target/thread semantics, and errors.
Both UI processes demonstrate safe rendering, fragmented-stream recovery, explicit caller switching, and independent consumption.
Actual persisted H3 publication/subscription, UI-close host lifetime, stop/restart, and backup/restore pass against the candidate package.
All A01-A50 have current passing evidence with the relevant platform/method; missing/skipped/unexecuted required checks cannot count as pass.
Normal-operation compiler/analyzer/package/runtime/browser warnings and review findings are zero; injected negative outcomes are explicitly asserted.
Candidate commit, effective configuration, dependency versions, product hashes, and evidence are recorded; the separate M06 full review is still required.
